title: URLCode request fixtures
description: tests/requests.json, replayed by `urlcode test` and `urlcode audit`: an array of request cases and ordered `steps` fixtures. Unknown keys are rejected. See https://github.com/jimhoyd-com/urlcode/blob/v0.6.5/docs/READINESS.md.

path.description: Local request target starting with /, such as /api/items?limit=2. Inside steps it may start with a {{name}} captured by an earlier step. Any case may use {{origin}}, the site origin, in path, headers, body, expectHeaders and expectBody (for example "origin": "{{origin}}" on an unsafe request to an auth: true route).

body.description: Request body text. A JSON body is a JSON string, such as "{\"name\":\"Ada\"}", sent with headers {"content-type": "application/json"}.

expectHeaders.description: Expected response header values, each compared exactly; names are case-insensitive.

expectBody.description: Expected response body, compared exactly as UTF-8 text. To assert some values of a JSON body, use expectJson.

expectJson.description: JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) into the JSON response body and the value each must equal, such as {"/balance": 100, "/items/0/done": false}; objects compare regardless of key order, arrays in order, and anything the map does not name (generated ids, timestamps) is not checked. "" is the whole body. A string may use {{name}} references; inside steps, a string that is exactly one reference to a number or boolean a json capture kept stands for that number or boolean.

expectSignals.description: Signals this request must emit, checked by `urlcode test` and `urlcode audit`, which record signals in process and deliver none. Each entry counts the captured signals it matches: exactly `count` when given, else at least one. An empty array expects no signal at all. Signals the list does not mention are allowed. `urlcode verify-deployment` cannot observe a deployment's signals and reports these as not checked. See https://github.com/jimhoyd-com/urlcode/blob/v0.6.5/docs/EGRESS.md.

destination.description: The signal's destination origin, exactly as `urlcode permissions` grants it (https://hooks.example.com).

count.description: Exactly this many matching signals. Absent: at least one.

match.description: JSON Pointers into the signal payload {version, route, status, method} and the value each must equal exactly, such as {"/status": 202, "/route": "/contact"}.

capture.description: Values kept from this step's response for later steps' {{name}} references: {"json": "items.0.id"}, {"header": "location"} (one single-valued header, never set-cookie) or {"cookie": "session"} (the value the fixture's cookie jar holds for that cookie after this response). `urlcode test` failure output shows json and header values where they were substituted; add "secret": true to a json or header capture that holds a credential (a token) to keep it out, as a cookie value always is.

secret.description: Never show this json or header value in failure output; it is printed as {{name}}.

headers.description: Request headers. The fixture's cookie jar adds the cookies earlier steps' responses set; an explicit cookie header is sent as written and the jar adds only the cookies it does not name.
